payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a vault repository commits, then tracker-path-scan scans the raw events of the unshared queue only, not the published view, with the match rule, path rule and holder exemption unchanged
When a new queued event holds the machine user name, then the commit is refused, also when its record is already published
When a published event holds the name and the queue is clean, then the commit is not blocked
When the queue cannot be read, then the scan falls back to the full view
payload.description:
## Context
When a vault repository commits, tracker-path-scan scans the whole published pending view, so one published note with the user name blocks every later commit and cannot be repaired. 2026-11-20 13:07 UTC: the 0.47.0 consumer proof for development was refused on vault/events-0001.jsonl:1100, a published Orchestrator note (dev-j6oqo#ev-e981e80250). Gate change decided by the Orchestrator 2026-11-20 13:16 UTC (record dev-j6oqo, entry [decision 2026-11-20 13:16 UTC], council run 13:15 UTC: safety, user and skeptic approve). Conditions: scan raw queue events, never record ids; fail closed to the full view; tests for a new event, a published event, a new event on a published record and the fail-closed path.
